originalTitle: Men are losing ground in the labor market. Here's why
summary: Women outnumbered men in the workforce for eight straight months as of September, according to one analysis.
content:
Friday's weaker-than-expected jobs report may feel especially lousy for men.

Women outnumbered men in the workforce for eight straight months as of September, according to an analysis of government data by Indeed. That's the longest stretch since 2010, the job search platform found.

"Back then, the gap emerged because men were losing jobs," said Cory Stahle, senior economist at Indeed. "This time, it's because women are gaining them."

Across the board, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Friday that U.S. payrolls grew by 29,000 jobs on net in September, lower than economists consensus forecast for an increase of 84,000.

Men represented slightly over half of net job growth in September, according to a CNBC analysis of Friday's BLS data. A month prior, men represented just 2% of payroll growth.

Despite the monthly increase, the seasonally adjusted number of employed men in the U.S. was lower by about 1.2 million in September compared with a year ago. Women's employment rose by more than 650,000 in the same period.

This divergence in labor market performance by gender can be partially explained by which industries are growing, according to Stahle.

Healthcare , a key driver of the U.S. job market for the last several years, accounted for more than half of overall payroll expansion in September. Women make up nearly four out of every five workers in the sector.

But the BLS said in its Friday release that healthcare hired at a slower pace in September than on average over the past year. Because of that, women may not have gotten as big of a boost from the sector as they did in prior months.

Monthly payroll contraction in industries with a higher share of women workers like government also diluted overall gains for women in the month, Stahle said.
chineseTitle: 男性在劳动力市场上正在节节败退。这就是为什么
chineseSummary: 一项分析显示，截至 9 月份，劳动力中女性人数连续八个月超过男性。
chineseContent:
周五弱于预期的就业报告对男性来说可能尤其糟糕。

根据 Indeed 对政府数据的分析，截至 9 月份，女性劳动力人数连续八个月超过男性。该求职平台发现，这是自 2010 年以来最长的一次。

Indeed 高级经济学家科里·斯塔勒 (Cory Stahle) 表示：“当时，差距的出现是因为男性失业。” “这一次，是因为女性正在赢得它们。”

美国劳工统计局周五表示，美国 9 月份就业岗位净增长 29,000 个，低于经济学家普遍预测的增长 84,000 个。

根据 CNBC 对周五劳工统计局数据的分析，男性占 9 月份净就业增长的一半以上。一个月前，男性仅占工资增长的 2%。

尽管月度增长，但经季节调整后，美国 9 月份就业男性人数仍较去年同期减少约 120 万人。同期，女性就业人数增加了 65 万人以上。

斯塔勒表示，劳动力市场表现的性别差异可以部分解释为哪些行业正在增长。

医疗保健是过去几年美国就业市场的主要驱动力，占 9 月份总体薪资增长的一半以上。该行业近五分之四的工人都是女性。

但美国劳工统计局在周五发布的新闻稿中表示，9 月份医疗保健部门的招聘速度低于过去一年的平均水平。正因为如此，女性可能没有像前几个月那样从该行业获得那么大的推动。

斯塔勒表示，政府等女性员工比例较高的行业的月度工资收缩也稀释了女性本月的总体收益。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
